blocks.body: # Luke Motion Correction and Spike Recovery

## Technical summary

Luke genuinely moves more than Yates, but full non-rigid voltage warps from both DREDGE and MEDiCINe are causal failures: they more than double learned detections and coincidence while reducing recovery. Zero-displacement interpolation is byte-identical to no correction, localizing the catastrophe to applied depth-dependent displacement rather than a generic export path.

The original Luke--Yates per-channel deficit was also denominator-confounded because Luke has 3.41x more contacts per millimetre. Per physical depth, Luke's no-motion unit density and coincidence are similar to Yates and Kilosort recovers nearly all strong input events. Luke still has about half as many strong negative events per millimetre, an upstream density difference that remains unexplained.

No external voltage correction remains the production baseline. Single-pass Kilosort conditioning is the leading preprocessing candidate, but its higher unit yield is partly nearby-template redundancy and requires a matched full-session merge/continuity audit.

## The original per-channel deficit was denominator-confounded

Luke has 3.41x more contacts per millimetre than Yates. Per physical depth, Luke has similar unit density and near-identical coincidence, while Kilosort recovers 94--96% of strong negative input events versus 97% in Yates. Luke still has about half as many such events per millimetre; that is an upstream density difference, not a large sorter miss rate.

## Reference changes are null; single-pass conditioning is promising

Removing local reference, substituting global reference, or disabling Kilosort CAR does not improve fixed-event recovery. In the independent 240 s window, a single Kilosort high-pass/CAR pass reduces learned detections by 10.9%, raises KS-good units from 130 to 168, and slightly improves reviewed recovery and coincidence.

## Much of the single-pass unit gain is redundant

The 101-unit raw increase includes 68 additional redundant nodes in a nearby-template similarity graph. Effective all-unit graph components rise only 14%, while good-unit components rise 23%. The condition may improve separation, but it also over-splits and must be compared after identical merging.

## Luke has a real motion problem

In matched 120-second summaries, MEDiCINe gives Luke rigid excursions of 13.1 and 14.7 µm versus about 3 µm for Yates. Kilosort-style estimates give 5.8 and 10.1 µm for Luke versus 0.75--1.0 µm median Yates values. Luke's larger movement and speed reproduce across estimator families.

## The interpolation scale is probe-dependent

At a 2 µm shift, the default 20 µm kriging kernel leaves a median maximum weight of 0.914 on Luke versus 0.962 on Yates. A 10 µm kernel improves Luke event peak retention from 96.6% to 97.7% and restores 127 KS-good units versus 115 at sigma 20, but remains below the no-correction quality safeguard.

## The supported non-rigid scale is approximately 300--400 µm

The 300/200 residual field is reproducible across random peak halves, unchanged by denser 100 µm sampling, and supported by the decentralized estimator. The 600 µm family is internally stable but loses simultaneous-probe residual agreement, consistent with smoothing away supported local structure.

## Channel-to-geometry mapping is exact across all representations

Raw SpikeGLX, saved processed metadata, and Kilosort each contain 384 neural channels. Raw and processed channel IDs are identical in row order, every coordinate agrees with a maximum error of 0 µm, and the best geometry assignment is the identity for 384/384 rows. The acquisition metadata independently records AP0--AP383 sequentially and reproduces the same four-column lateral stagger. This substantially downgrades mapping error as the cause.

## The raw-waveform alarm is a checksum failure, not a mapping result

The attached audit averages unconditioned raw voltage, causing row 216 to dominate multiple unrelated units. After filtering and local referencing, the dominant row becomes 191—the single channel already classified as bad and interpolated upstream. Reproducing that interpolation still leaves several pathological-sort units noncompact, but the same recurring row-216 signal affects the no-correction control. KS-good labels from these problematic sorts are therefore not independent biological ground truth for mapping.

## Zero-displacement interpolation is an exact identity

The 2.764 GB zero-motion trace binary is byte-for-byte identical to the no-correction input. Six checked Kilosort outputs are also exact byte matches: spike times, clusters, positions, learned detections, KS labels, and contamination. This rules out damage from the application/export machinery when displacement is exactly zero.

## Nonzero motion introduces two distinct failures

No correction and zero-motion identity recover 23/27 events. Kilosort internal rigid recovers 22/27 without collision inflation. Full external rigid recovers 20/27. DREDGE 300/200 recovers 18/27 and MEDiCINe recovers 19/27; both more than double learned detections and coincidence. Depth-dependent voltage warping, not one estimator, drives overdecomposition.

## Reduced rigid gain is mechanistically useful but not a production winner

Rigid gains 0.25 and 0.50 recover 24/27 events in the selection window, but the 0.25 benefit does not replicate on the strict automatic cohort in an independent 240-second window. A narrower 10 µm kernel reduces attenuation and restores most good-unit yield, yet contamination remains 9.9 points above baseline. No external correction remains the safest baseline.

## Kilosort's internal rigid estimate is motion-like but discontinuous

After sign alignment, its temporal shape correlates 0.80 with DREDGE. But Kilosort has 3.9× the temporal variance, a 128.5 µm peak-to-peak range, and ten adjacent 2 s jumps above 50 µm; DREDGE has none. Local code inspection shows temporal smoothing is applied only after unsmoothed coarse alignment shifts have already accumulated, making coarse mode switches a plausible Luke-specific failure.

## Full-field misses occur at larger fitted motion and spatial gradient

The nine selected-correction misses have twice the median absolute spatial gradient of the 18 recovered events (0.016 versus 0.008 µm/µm). Absolute displacement is also larger. This descriptive, post hoc association is consistent with the rigid-only result: spatial gradients amplify failure, although rigid resampling still causes losses.

## Scope, data, and definitions

The cohort is 27 blinded-review neural events originally unmatched in Luke imec1 from 8,160--8,280 s. All downstream conditions use the same current-conditioned input, Kilosort settings, probe geometry, and disabled claim mask. Recovery requires a final spike within 0.5 ms and 100 µm.

## Methodology

Motion fields were placed on a common 2 s by 200 µm grid and decomposed into rigid, linear-depth, and residual components. External rigid conditions repeat the depth mean across all bins at gains 0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, and 1. Identity sets every displacement to zero. All externally processed conditions use float interpolation, `force_zeros`, int16 saving, and unchanged claim-off Kilosort. Internal rigid reads the untouched binary with `do_correction=True, nblocks=1`.

## Limitations and robustness

The fixed-event cohorts are descriptive and Kilosort labels are not ground truth. Per-depth normalization removes the largest probe-density confound, but Luke and Yates still use different probe geometries and may sample different laminar populations. The exact legacy Yates preprocessing graph is unavailable. The template-similarity graph uses a declared 0.8 correlation and 100 micrometre neighborhood and does not replace matched merging.

## Recommended next steps

1. Keep no external voltage correction as the Luke production baseline.
2. Run a matched full-session current-versus-single-pass conditioning comparison with identical merging and unit-family continuity checks.
3. Do not use full non-rigid DREDGE or MEDiCINe warps; both recreate overdecomposition.
4. If interpolation is revisited, scale the kernel to probe geometry and require strict recovery, contamination, and collision safeguards.
5. Replace per-channel Luke--Yates comparisons with physical-depth and matched-layer denominators; use a common raw detector to locate the remaining negative-event density difference.
6. Prefer motion-aware coordinate/template tracking that avoids resampling raw voltage.

## Further questions

- Is Luke's lower strong-negative event density already present in matched raw AP voltage and comparable laminar bands?
- Does single-pass conditioning retain its 23% increase in good similarity-graph components after identical merging over the full session?
- What property of Luke's spike fingerprint makes Kilosort coarse registration switch between modes separated by 70--103 micrometres?

charts.title: Residual-field validation correlations
charts.description: The 300/200 candidate is the only family supported by all four validation lanes.

query.description: Select the candidate validation rows used in the grouped comparison.
query.sql: SELECT candidate, criterion, correlation, probe_basis FROM read_csv_auto('testing/outputs/luke_motion_candidate_results/spatial_scale_evidence.csv') ORDER BY criterion, candidate

charts.title: Reviewed neural-event recovery
charts.description: Same 27 prespecified events and identical sorter settings across conditions.

query.description: Select all fixed correction conditions and their recovery values.
query.sql: SELECT condition, observed_recovery AS recovery_fraction, learned_detection_count, cross_unit_near_coincident_fraction, median_contamination_pct, n_ks_good FROM read_csv_auto('testing/outputs/luke_motion_candidate_results/motion_candidate_sorter_metrics.csv') ORDER BY observed_recovery DESC

charts.title: Reviewed event recovery across rigid gain
charts.description: Same DREDGE depth-mean trace scaled from zero to full amplitude; 27 fixed events.

query.description: Select the five external rigid-gain conditions in gain order.
query.sql: SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto('testing/outputs/luke_motion_candidate_results/motion_candidate_sorter_metrics.csv') WHERE condition IN ('No external correction','Rigid gain 0.25','Rigid gain 0.50','Rigid gain 0.75','Rigid from 300/200') ORDER BY CASE condition WHEN 'No external correction' THEN 0 WHEN 'Rigid gain 0.25' THEN 1 WHEN 'Rigid gain 0.50' THEN 2 WHEN 'Rigid gain 0.75' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END

charts.title: Strong negative Kilosort-input events by physical depth
charts.description: Median physically deduplicated 6-sigma events per sampled millimetre and second; 60 two-second batches per condition.

query.description: Select the four reviewed condition summaries after physical-depth normalization.
query.sql: SELECT dataset AS condition, negative_6sigma_events_per_depth_mm_s AS negative_events_per_mm_s, negative_6sigma_final_recovery, learned_per_depth_mm_s, final_per_depth_mm_s, units_per_depth_mm, cross_unit_near_coincident_fraction FROM read_csv_auto('testing/outputs/luke_motion_candidate_results/luke_yates_detection_stage_dataset_metrics.csv') ORDER BY dataset
metric_definitions: Negative events are physically deduplicated local minima exceeding six batch-specific MAD units per sampled millimetre and second.

tables.title: Matched 120-second motion summaries
tables.description: Luke values are the prespecified pathological window; Yates values are medians across non-overlapping reference windows.

source.label: Luke and Yates matched-duration motion comparison

query.description: Summarize Luke directly and Yates by the median of non-overlapping 120-second windows for each estimator and probe.
query.sql: SELECT estimator, dataset || ' ' || probe AS recording, MEDIAN(rigid_excursion_p95_p5_um) AS rigid_excursion_um, MEDIAN(median_nonrigid_spread_um) AS median_spread_um, MEDIAN(p99_rigid_speed_um_per_s) AS p99_speed_um_s FROM read_csv_auto('testing/outputs/luke_motion_candidate_results/luke_yates_motion_120s_metrics.csv') GROUP BY estimator, dataset, probe ORDER BY estimator, dataset, probe

tables.title: Geometry-dependent interpolation weights
tables.description: Median maximum source-channel coefficient at selected displacements.

query.description: Pivot selected displacement and bandwidth rows for the two probe geometries.
query.sql: SELECT shift_um, MAX(CASE WHEN probe='Luke imec1' AND sigma_um=20 THEN median_peak_weight END) AS luke_sigma20, MAX(CASE WHEN probe='Yates shank' AND sigma_um=20 THEN median_peak_weight END) AS yates_sigma20, MAX(CASE WHEN probe='Luke imec1' AND sigma_um=10 THEN median_peak_weight END) AS luke_sigma10 FROM read_csv_auto('testing/outputs/luke_motion_candidate_results/luke_yates_interpolation_kernel_metrics.csv') WHERE shift_um IN (1,2,4,6) GROUP BY shift_um ORDER BY shift_um

tables.title: Sorter outcomes and guardrails
tables.description: Fixed 120-second imec1 window; lower learned detections, coincidence, and contamination are safeguards rather than objectives alone.

query.description: Select recovery and sorter guardrails for all correction conditions.
query.sql: SELECT condition, CAST(ROUND(observed_recovery * n_events) AS INTEGER) AS recovered, learned_detection_count AS learned_detections, cross_unit_near_coincident_fraction AS coincidence_fraction, median_contamination_pct, n_ks_good AS ks_good_units FROM read_csv_auto('testing/outputs/luke_motion_candidate_results/motion_candidate_sorter_metrics.csv') ORDER BY recovered DESC

tables.title: Rigid gain response and safeguards
tables.description: Gain zero is no external correction; gain one is the full DREDGE depth mean.

query.description: Select the five external rigid-gain outcomes in gain order.
query.sql: SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto('testing/outputs/luke_motion_candidate_results/motion_candidate_sorter_metrics.csv') WHERE condition IN ('No external correction','Rigid gain 0.25','Rigid gain 0.50','Rigid gain 0.75','Rigid from 300/200')

tables.title: Rigid-estimator temporal stability
tables.description: Both traces sampled at the same 60 Kilosort batch centers; Kilosort sign-aligned and each trace median-centered for shape statistics.

source.label: Kilosort and DREDGE rigid trace comparison

query.description: Aggregate temporal stability metrics for the two rigid estimators.
query.sql: SELECT 'Kilosort internal rigid' AS estimator, STDDEV_SAMP(kilosort_sign_aligned_centered_um) AS std_um, MAX(kilosort_sign_aligned_centered_um)-MIN(kilosort_sign_aligned_centered_um) AS peak_to_peak_um, MAX(kilosort_abs_step_um) AS max_step_um, SUM(CASE WHEN kilosort_abs_step_um > 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS steps_over_50_um FROM read_csv_auto('testing/outputs/luke_motion_candidate_results/internal_rigid_trace_comparison.csv') UNION ALL SELECT 'DREDGE rigid', STDDEV_SAMP(dredge_rigid_centered_um), MAX(dredge_rigid_centered_um)-MIN(dredge_rigid_centered_um), MAX(dredge_abs_step_um), SUM(CASE WHEN dredge_abs_step_um > 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM read_csv_auto('testing/outputs/luke_motion_candidate_results/internal_rigid_trace_comparison.csv')

tables.title: Selected-field motion at reviewed events
tables.description: Descriptive medians for the 27 fixed events, grouped by selected-correction outcome.

source.label: Paired reviewed-event recovery and motion covariates

query.description: Aggregate selected-correction event motion by recovery outcome.
query.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN recovered THEN 'Recovered' ELSE 'Missed' END AS outcome, COUNT(*) AS n_events, MEDIAN(selected_abs_displacement_um) AS median_abs_displacement_um, MEDIAN(selected_abs_spatial_gradient_um_per_um) AS median_abs_gradient FROM read_csv_auto('testing/outputs/luke_motion_candidate_results/reviewed_event_recovery.csv') WHERE condition = 'Selected DREDGE 300/200' GROUP BY recovered ORDER BY outcome

tables.title: Channel mapping reconciliation
tables.description: All 384 neural-channel rows; exact means zero coordinate difference without tolerance.

source.label: Luke imec1 channel and geometry mapping audit

query.description: Reconcile raw, processed, and Kilosort row geometry across all neural channels.
query.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_compared, SUM(CASE WHEN raw_channel_id = processed_channel_id THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS exact_channel_ids, SUM(CASE WHEN raw_x_um = processed_x_um AND raw_y_um = processed_y_um THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS raw_processed_exact_geometry_rows, SUM(CASE WHEN raw_x_um = kilosort_x_um AND raw_y_um = kilosort_y_um THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS raw_kilosort_exact_geometry_rows, MAX(GREATEST(ABS(raw_x_um - processed_x_um), ABS(raw_y_um - processed_y_um), ABS(raw_x_um - kilosort_x_um), ABS(raw_y_um - kilosort_y_um))) AS max_coordinate_error_um FROM read_csv_auto('testing/outputs/luke_geometry_mapping_audit/imec1/channel_mapping_rows.csv')

tables.title: Depth-normalized input and sorter comparison
tables.description: Same event detector and physical-depth denominator across conditions.

query.description: Select the four reviewed condition summaries after physical-depth normalization.
query.sql: SELECT dataset AS condition, negative_6sigma_events_per_depth_mm_s AS negative_events_per_mm_s, negative_6sigma_final_recovery, learned_per_depth_mm_s, final_per_depth_mm_s, units_per_depth_mm, cross_unit_near_coincident_fraction FROM read_csv_auto('testing/outputs/luke_motion_candidate_results/luke_yates_detection_stage_dataset_metrics.csv') ORDER BY dataset
metric_definitions: Negative events are physically deduplicated local minima exceeding six batch-specific MAD units per sampled millimetre and second.

tables.title: Reference and preprocessing ablations
tables.description: Fixed 120 s causal ablations plus independent 240 s single-pass replication.

query.description: Read the reviewed 120-second stage ablations and independent 240-second replication summary.
query.sql: SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto('testing/outputs/luke_motion_candidate_results/conditioning_replication_summary.csv') ORDER BY window, condition

tables.title: Unit yield versus nearby-template redundancy
tables.description: Similarity >=0.8 within 100 micrometres; graph components are a conservative effective-yield proxy.

query.description: Compare temporal stability and nearby-template similarity graph summaries for current and single-pass sorts.
query.sql: SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto('testing/outputs/luke_motion_candidate_results/luke_preprocessing_unit_structure_summary.csv') ORDER BY unit_scope, condition
metric_definitions: Similar pairs have template correlation at least 0.8 and peak positions within 100 micrometres.
